Is this normal?

My parents have both been with me for three weeks now to help my mom get through her radiation and chemo. I’m here all day helping. In this short time I’m noticing my dad doing things that I just can’t believe and that worry me. For example, walking away from the fridge leaving the door wide open while it’s beeping to notify it’s open, walking away from the garden hose that is on full blast and not hearing or seeing that he left it running. The other day he also hit my garage door while parking. Is this just normal cognitive decline for an 80 yr old and how do you deal when you’re scared to even leave them unattended in your home? These mishaps are practically daily and I can only imagine if I wasn’t here to catch it all as it happens.

Allowing parent with dementia to visit the family home they can no longer live in.

My sister and I have a parent (mother - mid 80's) who has dementia, and it has progressed to a point where residential dementia care is necessary.   Her husband (our father) passed away around 10 years ago, and she has been living in the home independently.   Incidents over the last few months (her flooding the house, not eating, not bathing, becoming highly disorientated, significant memory issues, various safety issues) lead us to having her assessed by her long term Primary Doctor (who she has seen for well over a decade) plus a separate hospital appointed provider.  We also activated her enduring power of attorney.   She has been assessed as needing residential dementia care and living at home is not an option at all.   She is physically very fit for her age and in good physical health (she will quite happily walk for 30 minutes at a time - is active in her garden for hours at a time etc.)

Added complexity I live in the US, but my mother is in New Zealand.  My sister lives very close to her in NZ (10 minutes) from our mother.

We are lucky enough that selling her home of 40+ years is not necessary.  In fact we may decide to keep her house and rent it out at some point (not in immediate term) to generate ongoing income to offset care costs. We have resources to pay for our mother's care longer term (several years at least, and possibly indefinitely if we add in rental income to the mix - our father did an excellent job setting her up for retirement.... thanks Dad where ever you are!).   Point being her home will likely be accessible for a long time to come.

**Question: As we move mom to residential dementia care, should we let her visit back to her home at all,  or is making it a clean break a better choice.**   

This has happened suddenly so she really hasn't been back since the flood - save for gathering some belongings for a few hours before repairs even started.  It seems unfair to not let her visit - it truely was a family home and she was very house proud.  Since the flood she has been at my sister's house, then a temporary residential care facility and a hospital for the assessment. We understand how it could impact her ability to adjust to a residential dementia care facility and potentially be very upsetting.   We are looking for perspectives on allowing her to return to visit could help/hurt her transition.   My sister and I can see both sides of this and are interested in other's experiences.  Mom keeps saying she wants to return home, which is heartbreaking.

For the next month as we repair the flood damage to her house, it is unlivable anyway (some asbestos ceiling materials were discovered by the insurance company's builder so there is a lot of remediation work required to remove that during repairs - luckily we had great insurance on the house.....).  We have been thinking whether taking her home to see how big the repairs are may help set the tone that returning home isn't an option.

Everything in step father's name and he won't let my mom move to safety. 

I did a search to find something similar, apologies if this has already been discussed at length. 

My question is if there is anything I can do as it seems like my mother doesn't have any rights to use to advocate for change. 

The details: 

I live in Canada.


My mom (79) and step father (82) live in their dream house in the forest about 3 hours from me. They are on acreage* in woods outside a small town. Nearest hospital is 45 min in either direction. *If anything happened to them there is likely no way to get help as if they are home alone, injured, they couldn't obvs get to a phone, and there's aren't any neighbours or friends to notice if there aren't at events or whatever. They would just die and no one would notice. 

Step dad is a stubborn chauvinist.  He insisted my mom stop working when they married and he controls everything. Their marriage is awful (my mom isn't innocent in this, she's toxic grin depression of being in this marriage for 40 years.) 

Everything is in my step father's name. House, car, investments. She does not know where the will is and he won't show it to her (gaslights her if she asks). 


She has fallen twice in the last 3 months, all due to losing her footing on logical things* and not being able to recover quickly to avoid a fall. Meaning it is not neurological decline that made her fall, but genuine tripping. (She tripped in the brick edging in one of their garden beds, or in the hose on the pathway, and finally when the dog got tangled in her legs while she was making dinner.) In all three falls he was not home. With the two outside ones she hit her head but didn't lose consciousness and eventually managed to crawl to the house and recover. Had she passed out she would have died (or at least gotten very very sick) as it was very cold and raining and he wouldn't have seen her body when he came home, due to location.  

She is not safe to continue living there but he refuses to move. His parents are buried (ashes) on the property. He built the freaking house. He has ZERO plan to ever move out any awareness that he might not be able to live there 'forever'. I cannot afford to buy the land from him so it "stays in the family" (it's worth millions). 

She would like to move to an apt near me. Community, family, living in a city with resources for her ... 

I have POA for her, we set that up about ten years ago when he refused to show her the will. But of course it just covers her health care decisions (in the event the hospital even calls me). 

I know from others who's parent has died and everything is not in both of their names, that getting access to anything (funds, accounts) can take years (is this probate?) and until that time I'd need to cover her finances (which I don't have the $ to do).  

I lie in bed thinking about what to do here and I never come up with anything. 

If I talk to him about putting things in both their names he'll say no ("she's awful with money") and he'll get mad at her for telling me how things are in their marriage. I think as her kid that I have the right to know (as does she for crying out loud) what provisions have been made in the event that he dies first. Where the will is. Who his lawyer is. What his build area like each month. Basic stuff that shouldn't be so guarded. 
 
This has been the situation for decades and I would just go round and round in my head but never do anything because of the reasons above. (I mean really, what can I "do"?). 

But now that she's fallen multiple times and luckily not had worse outcomes, and she wants to move, I feel like this need to change and things need to be said. 

But I'm pretty sure she has zero 'rights' in this situation, and without access to her own money can't leave anyway. 

Is there anything I can do that I haven't considered? 

Thanks for reading all of this.

Increasing anxiety phone calls from mother

My mother, 93 with short-term memory loss, relies on me for most things at this point, and a pattern that's gone through the roof this week is odd phone calls asking if I'm OK. I rent the house next door to her, and she just called me at midnight because "your lights were still on." It's perfectly normal for my porch lights to be on at midnight. On Sunday, I went to an afternoon concert and told her I might be a little later than usual getting back to get her dinner, but emphasized that I would be there and NOT TO CALL ASKING WHERE I WAS. I emphasized that to her, and she answered, "OK." The phone calls started when I was driving home on the highway in the dark in pouring rain. I didn't feel safe answering the phone because I didn't want to take my eyes off the road (my car is too old to have Bluetooth links to a cell phone). She called three times. When I arrived home, a neighbor was sitting there with her. She had called the neighbor because she was so worried about me. I also keep a land line at home, and there were four messages on the answering machine there. 

It's getting out of control and making my life even more miserable than it already is. 

I guess it's because she lives alone with a cat, but it's like her anxieties build up until she starts imagining that something bad has happened to me and then talks herself into the idea that it has actually happened. 

Other than my constantly calling to reassure her (which I really don't want to have to do), are there any ideas on how to moderate this anxiety for her? I'm getting really angry about it.

Relative didn’t sign her will…

TLDR; relative didn’t sign her will and now my parent in the nursing home is being punished. 

Hi guys, I was a pretty active member of this sub until my parent transitioned to long term care last year, but I wanted to tell a cautionary tale. And I want to vent. 

Over the past two years, my mom’s sister has been talking to me about what she’s going to leave me in her will. She was going to leave me everything; life changing money. She died suddenly yesterday. 

Here comes the greedy relative part. Right? Not really. 

When she passed I made a quick call to the lawyer because there was something I need immediate information on (it was pet related). I’m the course of the conversation, they mentioned that I was her beneficiary—but as the title says, NEVER SIGNED THE WILL. 

This means that her asset will immediately transfer to her next of kin, my mom. Cool, right? Mom will get some extra cash, live like a princess and probably gift a few bucks to me. 

No. Mom is on Medicaid. So in essence, my Aunt worked her entire life only for the state to come in and take it. But it gets worse. Because of this increase in assets, mom will actually get kicked off Medicaid and have to go through the whole process again. 

The real kicker? She got a letter in the mail the day she went back into the hospital letting her know her will was never signed. 

I am so angry. She would have been better off leaving her entire estate to charity. My feelings aside, she would have never wanted to harm her sister financially. What a mess. 

Anyway, thank you for reading if you’ve gotten this far. Please, please check your loved ones documents. No matter what they said and promised, they are elderly and the system is stacked against them.

The Doctor thanked me

TW: wounds, bodily fluids

My mother has a sacral wound that I have been taking care of for almost 4 years.  It started at just under 12 inches in diameter.  It was necrotic.  I threw up the first time I saw it, as it looked like a wild animal had taken a massive bite out of her.  It required 3 times daily cleaning and packing (I was going through a dozen washclothes and towels a day to handle the volume of discharge)./.  I learned to use a wound vac and change the packing for that device (skills I'm told are usually only done by trained nurses).  When a closure was attempted, I had to drain the stints put in, and then deal with the fallout when the closure ruptured due to hospital incompetency.  I've had to roll her in bed every couple of hours and limit her activity and sitting upright.  I've had to carefully manage her diet and force her to eat as much protein as she can to heal the wound.  I've had to limit her sugars to manage her diabetes to help heal the wound.  I've had to deal with a gaping, bleeding, pussy, infected hole in my mother's lower back for years (in addition to everything else).

Today, at her wound check-in, the Doctor thanked me for all of that because he said she probably only had one more visit since it is basically healed.  He said that I had done everything right and that was what had helped it get to this point.  I've spent almost four years being "the bad guy," and it was very nice to hear that.

She's still half paralyzed.  She still has aphasia.  She still has incontinence issues.  

But tonight, I'm happy for actual, measurable, medical progress and recognition of my role in it.

Relationships & Support - how do you express your unmet needs, as a the caregiver, to your partner when they are always tired/overstimulated/depressed/unwell?

Couldn't think of a more elegant way of describing my question in the title.

Basically - I'm the caregiver to my partner (who has Crohn's, depression, and an ED) and I have been struggling. I'm sympathetic as someone who also has depression and has recovered from an ED myself - but I REALLY struggle with communicating my needs to her when I'm always either in caregiver mode or am burnt out by it myself.

I feel like I'm spending a lot of time tending to her needs while never having an opening to express my own. My history of CEN makes it very difficult for me to advocate for my own needs, even under ideal circumstances, so when my partner is seemingly always tired/struggling/etc I feel like I never have the opportunity to hold space for my own needs.

I love her to death and this is hard and lonely.

Every time I resolve myself to really open up to her on how lonely I feel (mostly verbal/non-verbal intimacy and affection - which I need and receiving very, very little of) she seems to hit a rough patch. And the rough patches don't end so much as they bleed into one another. So there's never time for us to hold space on what \*I\* need.

At this point it hardly seems valid to try: since SHE is the one who is suffering, not me. But its making my giving her \*consistent\* care and support more difficult over time.

And yet I feel as if I can't speak up - because it seems that she's never well enough to hear about it.

Critical Care Parents While Parenting Young Kids

I think I’m looking for advice on how to pull my head out of my butt. It’s been a tough year and I need some advice/perspective to stop acting like a victim.

I have two kids, two and 8 months. I work full time. My husband is amazing & supportive.

My father passed away in February this year, he was 68. He was an addict and hadn’t been a part of my life (other than awful voicemails & mailings) for about 8 years. I went so far to block his number and never respond to his blocked voicemails - they ranged from cussing me out to begging to meet my kids, sometimes in the same sentence. His passing nonetheless was awful and I’m feeling really guilty, especially about the fact he never got to meet my children. My husband & I agreed he couldn’t be around them for safety issues, amongst others. But I still feel an immense emptiness & longing for what could have been.

My mother & step-father got in a car accident two weeks ago (both around age 60). They have broken legs, broken sternums, and my mom has a broken neck. My mom had a pre-existing eye problem and is essentially blind in one eye, and now the other eye is very spotty. She also previously had a couple vertebrae fused, and had knee problems (recurring cortisone injections, arthritis, braces, etc). 

My mom & step-dad just relocated to be near my family since we have the only grandkids. We have no other family (on my side of the family) anywhere near us. Except a younger sibling who is no help. My mom was an amazing grandma and lived for our kids. It was magical. Now I fear she will never be able to help us, and in fact we will have to help them. They moved into a gorgeous home, but not a ranch. With no main-floor bath (only powder room). My step-dad has no children & no interest in them. He is very kind and tolerant, but has no understanding of kids. He has been incredibly generous with his time and sharing my mom to be such an amazing grandma.

Since the accident I have been the only caregiver. My sibling took a 3 week trip abroad, 2 days after this accident. I work full time, but have been spending every single waking minute bedside at the ICU (bouncing between the hospital rooms since they’re in separate areas) when I am not actively taking care of my children. I am exhausted and fearful I will lose my job, husband, sanity.

Have you dealt with aging parents while being a young parent yourself? I always know it could be worse. Looking for hope. Thanks.

Extreme burnout post. Am I overreacting?

Hi and first of all thanks for taking your time to read this. I honestly don’t know where to vent, to cry or to ask for empathy anymore as this ‘guard’ caught me young, unprepared and definitely not physically or mentally ready, if one can ever be one of those 4 things when the time for caregiving comes. So thanks again for passing by. And thanks for caring.

I’ll give you the briefest version of this. 

I started dating my boyfriend -now husband- 11 years ago, when he was 20. He has neuropathic damage due to an injury that wasn’t treated or discovered for +7y so when we finally managed to push doctors to get a real diagnosis, it was already too late for a recovery. He lives with such an amount of pain that he needs an implant in the column + more than 10 pills per day just to bear it. Just to be able to exist. And the expectations for the future for him is ‘he would be deteriorating even more, until he dies’. So no real room for improvement. He is officially disabled in terms of mobility too and he can’t work. So I’m the only income. In addition and just to make things clear I love him and he is the most empathic, clever and lovable person I have ever met in all my life. Meeting him is still the best thing that has ever happened to me.

Now about me. 

- I’m 3 years older than him (so 34 now), have been working on media/games/teaching for +13y. My industry is so f up we have had to emigrate once and the average of my jobs are 2.5y before the company crashes (pretty normal in my industry). 

I mostly try to work remotely but I have been unemployed for 1y already and I’ll have to start working onsite soon, somewhere, somehow. As I’m the only income and we haven’t qualified for any official help, my salary has somehow to support us both. I have been teaching and tried anything that relates to my field on bad times but honestly not even libraries want to hire me at this point. Mostly because I refuse to do overtimes, travels for work and so on anymore. I just can’t being a caregiver, and no one gives a sh.

About our ‘safe circle’: 

- My parents have always been abusive so we get zero support from them. Sadly I have to live near them so I have to meet them from time to time (not really my choice but they will harass me heavily if not, playing the victim). They don’t understand my caregiver duties because “we are so young for that” and they are the type of people that think ‘going to a company with a CV gets you a job’. My father in law has disappeared from the map (aka he doesn’t care about us) and my mother in law kinda helps us, but only on the legal procedures and money. She doesn’t want to know anything about his son’s pain or his real struggles as it’s ’too hard for her’ and makes her ‘suffer’. Clearly I do not. Anyway.

- Friends? Tell me another joke. Had some, but half of them thought my partner was faking it for attention and the other half was somehow jealous of the ‘attention’ I paid to my partner, and I quote ‘Always siding with him when he said he was tired or couldn’t go out’. So they ditched me.

- My own health is shit. My doctor refuses to investigate about my symptoms and I have changed it several times already. I also have an sports injury that has me with constant pain, mild compared to my husbands so I don’t really pay much attention to him.

- Home? I do have one, rented, as it’s impossible for us to buy one. We can barely afford the rent tho.

- Hobbies and pets: Had some hobbies, my health issues prevents me to do them for long periods of time and we can’t afford having any pet, even though we have wanted a cat for years.

- Looking for medical psychological help: Doesn’t work, don’t really have time neither. To this day I have had really bad luck with their advices too, which reminds me to a post I saw recently here called “doctor told me not to ruin my life”. Well that has been basically the main experience. “Your husband ruins your situation, get rid of it”.

So after all this rant my question is, am I really overreacting feeling that I’m near rock bottom? That nothing seems to work anymore in my life? That I absolutely deserve some rest? My partner usually insists that I should take care of myself but with nothing more than him in my life atm I don’t feel like a productive person. Like I should have the right to refuse interviews for shitty jobs and that I should endure anything just to get us out of this situation. But the thing is, the “situation” has been shit for years already and without a job I don’t even know how to start ‘thinking on myself’ when my main concerns are having a home, 3 meals and healthcare for him.

I’m just so tired.
Thanks for listening.

mom rapidly declining after medical emergency recently, dad giving up on life

This is really to vent and hopefully get some advice from others who can maybe relate. This will probably be a long post 🥲

My (29f) mom’s (67F) health has been declining fairly rapidly I would say within the past 2 years. My mom previously had a hairline fracture in her back, and fell pretty badly in 2020, which caused her fracture to get worse. My parents are both pretty bad alcoholics, and my mom has fallen many times since then which has basically made her close to immobile now, needing to walk around 24/7 with a walker and mostly not being able to stand for long periods of time.

Right before thanksgiving, my little sister ended up in the ER, and while my mom was sitting in the ER with her, she faints. She did not fall, a nurse so happened to be paying attention to her at that moment and was able to help, but she passed out for a little. She ended up getting admitted as well. After a series of tests and procedures, they find out my mom has a hernia in her esophagus and stomach ulcers. The doctors make it sound like it’s no big deal, and she should feel better after her surgery and all will be well and good. Wrong. My mom’s hernia and esophagus are fine, but she completely has dementia now. She isn’t horrible with long term memory, but her short term memory is very bad. To the point where she can’t maintain her own appointments, or keep track of anything. Before this happened, my mom had issues with mobility and maybe her memory wasn’t the sharpest, but nothing compared to this. She was still driving and taking care of her own doctors appointments, getting to and from by herself, just using a cane. She showered and got ready everyday.

Basically since her memory issues are now bad, she can obviously no longer drive. She has to use a walker now. She rarely gets out of her pajamas. She is peeing herself frequently. Where we live it’s pretty snowy right now, and with her back issues it’s very hard to get her out of the house. My siblings honestly seem very emotionally detached from this, and I feel like I’m the only one helping to keep her on track and I feel like I’m drowning with no help.

My dad (65m) is an extremely bad alcoholic who will likely drink himself to death and is so stubborn he can not be convinced otherwise. and is borderline useless when it comes to anything with my mom because he can’t be bothered by anything that doesn’t involve drinking.

I moved back in after a break up over year ago to stay here for a bit to save for a house and I cannot believe how rapid my parents decline has happened. When I moved in last year my mom was going to museums, restaurants, to the store, her appointments on her own and now on Mondays I take my mom out for a few hours to get her out of the house because she can’t go anywhere on her own. Now my parents are extremely codependent on me helping them do everything around the house and take care of them, I’m scared if I leave they are just going to neglect themselves further. I am so stressed. I never have a day of peace where I am not worried about either of them. I hate that they don’t care anymore and I hate that they are letting themselves go and making everything more hard for me instead of trying to quit drinking, eat healthier, live a better life. Instead they just stay in and they drink. My parents were always outgoing and social people. They literally don’t do anything now.

I try to talk to them. My mom insists she’s fine, she doesn’t want to burden me and to live my life as much as possible but that’s next to impossible to do while I’m watching my parents just give up. And they aren’t even that old!!!!

I know this was long and I appreciate anyone who reaD this. I’m sure I’ll post again at some point because I honestly could vent about this forever. Sorry if this is all over the place…there’s honestly a lot of moving parts.

Taking care of a parent while having Schizoaffective disorder

I experienced a painful situation yesterday because I told my parent that I'm tired of going and bringing them medication from the drug store. While I already did this several times and took care of her, she cried and went angry because of this. I went and brought the medication at the end but she is still sad.

My story of caregiving with her started almost 10 years ago. In my culture it is a normal thing to serve your parents even if they don't treat you in the way you deserve. She took me for granted for a long time during her illness with diabetes and foot amputation. During these 10 years, I started to have schizophrenia, then bipolar, and went to the psychiatric hospital twice. 

I don't know how to cover the main issue but, some relatives accused me that I am taking advantage of my illness so no one asks me for any help and this was so annoying. I dealt with wisdom and didn't respond to this. I talked to my therapist about this too and she gave enough support and guidance. My parent said she doesn't want me at home (I am the only one living with her, I'm a female, 25 yo, unemployed and not married). This makes me stressed to hear such things from her.

So for the last 5 years, she is doing housework in the wheelchair and I rarely contribute because I was traumatized in the past because of her treatment. However, I did therapy and this was getting treated gradually and I started to help and contribute to housework.

She is ill and deserves better care, but I wonder if I am really guilty. I did my best to treat my trauma, and I totally understand that I am in a country with a culture that doesn't consider mental illness as much as a physical one.

I remember too that I was doing all the housework when I was 15 and 16 while I had my studies. I remember that I had to skip my exams to help her in the hospital. I think I am not selfish...

Can we just normalize normal things people face as they get older?

I wasn’t really sure what to title this. But I just wish so many things were more normalized or had less stigma, especially things that are common for aged people. 

Both of my parents deal with incontinence, but my dad way worse and he has accidents pretty often because he doesn’t realize he needs to pee until it’s immediate. My heart breaks for him because I know he’s embarrassed and feels humiliated. 

I’m currently in the ER with him (he’s feeling fine but sodium was low at PCP’s - most likely caused by his incontinence meds so that’s amazing) and a nurse didn’t come in time and he had an accident. Now the front of his jeans are wet but he doesn’t want to change into a gown or put a pull up on. And as a side note because it pissed me off, the nurse went into his room as he was standing and peeing into the container to turn off his call light which made him even more embarrassed. 

I don’t know, I just wish we normalized things so they’d maybe be less embarrassing because it sucks to see a 75 year old man be humiliated by something he literally can’t control.
